claim: Lnc-Rewind is expressed in murine muscle stem cells (MuSCs).
source: Here, we functionally characterize a novel chromatin-associated long noncoding RNA (lncRNA), Lnc-Rewind, which is expressed in murine MuSCs and conserved in human.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that Lnc-Rewind is expressed in murine MuSCs, and this is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Lnc-Rewind is conserved in human.
source: Here, we functionally characterize a novel chromatin-associated long noncoding RNA (lncRNA), Lnc-Rewind, which is expressed in murine MuSCs and conserved in human.
evidence: Conservation is demonstrated through sequence identity analysis and expression data in human myoblasts shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Lnc-Rewind acts as an epigenetic regulator of MuSC proliferation and expansion.
source: We find that, in mouse, Lnc-Rewind acts as an epigenetic regulator of MuSC proliferation and expansion by influencing the expression of skeletal muscle genes and several components of the WNT (Wingless-INT) signalling pathway.
evidence: This is supported by EdU incorporation experiments (Figure 2E) and single myofiber assays (Figure 2F,G) showing reduced proliferation upon Lnc-Rewind depletion.

claim: Lnc-Rewind influences the expression of skeletal muscle genes.
source: We find that, in mouse, Lnc-Rewind acts as an epigenetic regulator of MuSC proliferation and expansion by influencing the expression of skeletal muscle genes and several components of the WNT (Wingless-INT) signalling pathway.
evidence: RNA-seq analysis identified 1088 differentially expressed genes upon Lnc-Rewind depletion, with enrichment in muscle system processes (Figure 2A,B,C).

claim: Lnc-Rewind influences the expression of several components of the WNT signalling pathway.
source: We find that, in mouse, Lnc-Rewind acts as an epigenetic regulator of MuSC proliferation and expansion by influencing the expression of skeletal muscle genes and several components of the WNT (Wingless-INT) signalling pathway.
evidence: GO term enrichment analysis showed 'regulation of Wnt signalling pathway' as a significant category (p-value=5.44E-4), with Wnt7b identified as a target.

claim: Wnt7b gene is a direct Lnc-Rewind target.
source: Among them, we identified the nearby Wnt7b gene as a direct Lnc-Rewind target.
evidence: This is supported by RNA/DNA-FISH showing colocalization (Figure 4D), anti-correlated expression patterns (Figure 3B), and rescue experiments (Figure 3D,E).

claim: Lnc-Rewind interacts with the G9a histone lysine methyltransferase.
source: We show that Lnc-Rewind interacts with the G9a histone lysine methyltransferase and mediates the in cis repression of Wnt7b by H3K9me2 deposition.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RIP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), CLIP (Figure 4A), and RNA pulldown (Figure 4B) experiments.

claim: Lnc-Rewind mediates the in cis repression of Wnt7b by H3K9me2 deposition.
source: We show that Lnc-Rewind interacts with the G9a histone lysine methyltransferase and mediates the in cis repression of Wnt7b by H3K9me2 deposition.
evidence: ChIP experiments show decreased H3K9me2 levels at the Wnt7b locus upon Lnc-Rewind depletion (Figure 4E).

claim: Lnc-Rewind overlaps pre-Mirlet7c-2 (mmu-let7c-2) and pre-Mirlet7b (mmu-let7b) genomic loci.
source: Among them, we focused on Lnc-Rewind, which is a lncRNA enriched in proliferating myoblasts and overlapping pre-Mirlet7c-2 (mmu-let7c-2) and pre-Mirlet7b (mmu-let7b) genomic loci (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is shown in the UCSC visualization in Figure 1A.

claim: A conserved transcriptional start site (TSS) exists in the human syntenic locus (hs_Lnc-Rewind).
source: An evolutionary conservation analysis performed by examining FANTOM5 datasets (Noguchi et al., 2017) revealed the existence of a conserved transcriptional start site (TSS) localized in the human (hs_Lnc-Rewind) syntenic locus (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by FANTOM5 CAGE data analysis and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The human and murine Lnc-Rewind loci exhibit an overall ~46% of (exonic and intronic) sequence identity.
source: This region exhibits an overall ~46% of (exonic and intronic) sequence identity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which is relatively high for lncRNAs.
evidence: Sequence alignment analysis is presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The human syntenic region is actively transcribed in proliferating human myoblasts.
source: Moreover, RNA-seq (Legnini et al., 2017; Figure 1B) and semiquantitative (sq)RT-PCR analyses (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) confirmed that, in proliferating human myoblasts, this region is actively transcribed.
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA-seq data (Figure 1B) and sqRT-PCR (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Spliced and unspliced Lnc-Rewind isoforms originate from the mouse and human loci.
source: To note, the distribution of the read coverage in both mouse and human revealed the existence of spliced and unspliced Lnc-Rewind isoforms originating from the two loci (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is shown by RNA-seq read coverage patterns in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Lnc-Rewind expression is high in proliferating C2C12 and MuSC-derived myoblasts.
source: Quantitative qRT-PCR analysis revealed that Lnc-Rewind expression is high in proliferating (GM) C2C12 and MuSC-derived myoblasts and significantly decreased in fully differentiated (DM) cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: qRT-PCR data is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Lnc-Rewind expression is significantly decreased in fully differentiated cells.
source: Quantitative qRT-PCR analysis revealed that Lnc-Rewind expression is high in proliferating (GM) C2C12 and MuSC-derived myoblasts and significantly decreased in fully differentiated (DM) cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: qRT-PCR data is shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Both spliced and unspliced Lnc-Rewind isoforms localize in the nuclear compartment.
source: Subcellular fractionation of cytoplasmic (Cyt) and nuclear (Nuc) fractions showed that both spliced and unspliced isoforms localizes in the nuclear compartment (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Subcellular fractionation followed by RT-PCR is shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Lnc-Rewind is specifically enriched to discrete chromatin foci.
source: Accordingly, RNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) experiments performed in both MuSC-derived myoblasts (Figure 1E,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F) and C2C12 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G) confirmed the nuclear localization of Lnc-Rewind and further revealed its specific enrichment to discrete chromatin foci.
evidence: RNA-FISH images are shown in Figure 1E,F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: Lnc-Rewind depletion led to the identification of 1088 differentially expressed genes (DEGs).
source: Under these conditions, we obtained ~70% reduction of Lnc-Rewind expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, lower panel), which led to the identification of a set of 1088 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) (p<0.05, GAP-SCR vs GAP-REW).
evidence: RNA-seq analysis identified DEGs shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Of the 1088 DEGs, 332 were upregulated and 756 downregulated upon Lnc-Rewind depletion.
source: Of these, 332 were upregulated and 756 downregulated in GAP-REW as compared to the GAP-SCR condition (Figure 2A, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is shown in the heatmap in Figure 2A and detailed in Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: DEGs were mostly associated with muscle cell physiology (skeletal muscle contraction, p-value=4.23E-6).
source: It emerged that DEGs were mostly associated with muscle cell physiology (skeletal muscle contraction, p-value=4.23E-6) (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: GO term enrichment analysis results are shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Lnc-Rewind depletion results in concomitant downregulation of Mirlet7b and Mirlet7c-2.
source: Of note, the analysis of Lnc-Rewind generated miRNAs (Mirlet7b and Mirlet7c-2) revealed that, although the lncRNA depletion results on their concomitant downregulation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), none of the upregulated transcripts that are also putative Mirlet7b and Mirlet7c-2 targets (~1% of the upregulated genes) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), belong to any of the GO enriched categories.
evidence: qRT-PCR data for miRNAs is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Genes encoding for different proteins involved in muscle contraction, such as myosins (i.e. Myh8, Myl1, Myh3) and troponins (i.e. Tnnt2, Tnnt1), were downregulated upon Lnc-Rewind depletion.
source: Of note, genes encoding for different proteins involved in muscle contraction, such as myosins (i.e. Myh8, Myl1, Myh3) and troponins (i.e. Tnnt2, Tnnt1) (Figure 2C), were downregulated.
evidence: Heatmap showing downregulation of these genes is presented in Figure 2C.

claim: Lnc-Rewind-depleted cells express lower levels of MyHC protein.
source: Accordingly, Lnc-Rewind-depleted cells express lower levels of MyHC protein (Figure 2D).
evidence: Western blot analysis is shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Lnc-Rewind depletion results in a decreased number of MuSC-derived myoblasts.
source: Moreover, morphological evaluation highlighted a decreased number of MuSC-derived myoblasts after Lnc-Rewind depletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), suggesting a primary defect in MuSC proliferation.
evidence: Cell counting data is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: EdU incorporation experiments revealed a striking reduction of proliferating MuSC-derived myoblasts upon depletion of Lnc-Rewind.
source: In line with this hypothesis, EdU incorporation experiments revealed a striking reduction of proliferating MuSC-derived myoblasts upon depletion of Lnc-Rewind (Figure 2E).
evidence: EdU incorporation assay results are shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The Ccnd3 gene encoding for Cyclin D3 was significantly downregulated in Lnc-Rewind-depleted cells at both transcript and protein levels.
source: Accordingly, the Ccnd3 gene encoding for Cyclin D3, a cyclin specifically involved in promoting transition from G1 to S phase, was significantly downregulated in Lnc-Rewind-depleted cells at both transcript (Figure 2—source data 1) and protein levels (Figure 2D).
evidence: RNA-seq data (Figure 2—source data 1) and Western blot (Figure 2D) show downregulation.

claim: MuSCs on single myofibres cultured for 96 hr gave rise to a decreased percentage of proliferating (Pax7+/Ki67+) progeny upon Lnc-Rewind downregulation.
source: In further support of this, MuSCs on single myofibres cultured for 96 hr gave rise to a decreased percentage of proliferating (Pax7+/Ki67+) progeny upon Lnc-Rewind downregulation (Figure 2F).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification on single myofibres is shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Quantification of Pax7+-derived clusters, pairs, or single MuSCs within each myofibre revealed a reduction of activated pairs and clusters upon Lnc-Rewind depletion.
source: Moreover, quantification of the number of Pax7+-derived clusters (composed of more than two nuclei), pairs (composed of two nuclei), or single MuSCs within each myofibre revealed a reduction of activated pairs and clusters upon Lnc-Rewind depletion (Figure 2G), suggesting a role for the lncRNA in sustaining MuSC activation and expansion.
evidence: Quantification data is shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Wnt7b transcriptional locus localizes only 100 kb upstream of Lnc-Rewind gene.
source: Intriguingly, Wnt7b transcriptional locus localizes only 100 kb upstream Lnc-Rewind gene (Figure 3A).
evidence: Genomic location is shown in the UCSC visualization in Figure 3A.

claim: Wnt7b expression was found upregulated at both transcript and protein levels upon Lnc-Rewind depletion.
source: Among them, we found Wnt7b, which expression was found upregulated at both transcript and protein levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Figure 2—source data 1), suggesting a role for Lnc-Rewind as a repressor of Wnt7b expression.
evidence: qRT-PCR and Western blot data are shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Lnc-Rewind and Wnt7b transcripts display a distinctive anti-correlated expression in FANTOM5 CAGE profiles.
source: Indeed, the inspection of the TSS usage among all the available murine samples (n = 1196, Figure 3—source data 1) revealed a distinctive anti-correlated expression between Lnc-Rewind and Wnt7b transcripts (Figure 3B, left panels).
evidence: TSS usage analysis is shown in Figure 3B with Spearman correlation coefficient R = -0.68.

claim: Other Lnc-Rewind-neighbouring genes, such as Cdpf1 and Atxn10, displayed no specific expression correlation with Lnc-Rewind.
source: In contrast, the other Lnc-Rewind-neighbouring genes, such as Cdpf1 and Atxn10, displayed no specific expression correlation (Figure 3B, right panels).
evidence: TSS usage analysis is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Wnt7b was the only gene that was significantly upregulated upon Lnc-Rewind depletion with a concomitant increase in WNT7b protein levels.
source: Of note, Wnt7b was the only gene that was significantly upregulated upon the lncRNA depletion with a concomitant increase in WNT7b protein levels (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: qRT-PCR data for neighboring genes is shown in Figure 3C, and protein data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Rescuing Wnt7b repression promoted an increase in the percentage of proliferating MuSC-derived myoblasts towards control levels.
source: Of note, rescuing Wnt7b repression promoted an increase in the percentage of proliferating MuSC-derived myoblasts towards control levels (Figure 3D).
evidence: EdU incorporation assay with rescue experiment is shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Restoration of Wnt7b repression on single myofibres was sufficient to restore the capacity of the associated MuSCs to properly activate and proliferate ex vivo.
source: Similarly, restoration of Wnt7b repression on single myofibres was sufficient to restore the capacity of the associated MuSCs to properly activate and proliferate ex vivo (Figure 3E), as assessed by the quantification of the number of Pax7+ MuSCs and the percentage of single MuSCs, and derived clusters and pairs, within each myofibre (Figure 3E).
evidence: Single myofibre rescue experiment data is shown in Figure 3E.

claim: EZH2 is mostly expressed in proliferating MuSCs and becomes downregulated during muscle differentiation.
source: Both EZH2 (Caretti et al., 2004) and G9a (Ling et al., 2012) are mostly expressed in proliferating MuSCs and become downregulated during muscle differentiation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), similarly to Lnc-Rewind (Figure 1C).
evidence: Western blot data is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, and this is supported by citations.

claim: G9a is mostly expressed in proliferating MuSCs and becomes downregulated during muscle differentiation.
source: Both EZH2 (Caretti et al., 2004) and G9a (Ling et al., 2012) are mostly expressed in proliferating MuSCs and become downregulated during muscle differentiation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), similarly to Lnc-Rewind (Figure 1C).
evidence: Western blot data is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, and this is supported by citations.

claim: EZH2 has been previously reported to be recruited to specific genomic loci through the interaction with different lncRNAs.
source: Moreover, both EZH2 (Rinn et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2008) and G9a (Nagano et al., 2008; Pandey et al., 2008) have been previously reported to be recruited to specific genomic loci through the interaction with different lncRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: G9a has been previously reported to be recruited to specific genomic loci through the interaction with different lncRNAs.
source: Moreover, both EZH2 (Rinn et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2008) and G9a (Nagano et al., 2008; Pandey et al., 2008) have been previously reported to be recruited to specific genomic loci through the interaction with different lncRNAs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Lnc-Rewind transcript was efficiently retrieved only in the G9a native RIP, while it was almost undetectable in EZH2 IP.
source: We observed that, although both G9a and EZH2 were successfully immunoprecipitated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, upper panel), Lnc-Rewind transcript was efficiently retrieved only in the G9a native RIP, while it was almost undetectable in EZH2 IP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, lower panel).
evidence: RIP experiment results are shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The levels of Lnc-Rewind RNA obtained in the G9a IP fraction were similar to the ones of the Kcnq1ot1 lncRNA.
source: To note, the levels of RNA obtained in the specific IP fraction were similar to the ones of the Kcnq1ot1 lncRNA, which was previously demonstrated to be physically associated with both G9a and Ezh2 proteins (Pandey et al., 2008).
evidence: This comparison is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and supported by citation.

claim: G9a-crosslinked immunoprecipitation (CLIP) assay revealed the presence of Lnc-Rewind in the G9a immunoprecipitated samples.
source: On the one hand, the G9a-crosslinked immunoprecipitation (CLIP) assay (Figure 4A) revealed the presence of Lnc-Rewind in the G9a immunoprecipitated samples.
evidence: CLIP experiment results are shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Endogenous Lnc-Rewind RNA pulldown revealed the presence of G9a in the lncRNA-precipitated fraction.
source: As a further validation, endogenous Lnc-Rewind RNA pulldown (Figure 4B) revealed the presence of G9a in the lncRNA-precipitated fraction.
evidence: RNA pulldown experiment results are shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Depletion of G9a by siRNA-mediated knockdown in MuSC-derived myoblasts induced Wnt7b upregulation.
source: In support of this, depletion of G9a by siRNA-mediated knockdown in MuSC-derived myoblasts induced Wnt7b upregulation (Figure 4C).
evidence: qRT-PCR data showing Wnt7b upregulation upon G9a knockdown is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: RNA-DNA-FISH showed an overlap between Lnc-Rewind (RNA) and Wnt7b (DNA) localization.
source: To test whether Lnc-Rewind and G9a binds the Wnt7b locus in vivo, we applied RNA-DNA-FISH (Figure 4D) and a chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), respectively. In agreement with our hypothesis, we found an overlap between Lnc-Rewind (RNA) and Wnt7b (DNA) localization (Figure 4D) and an intriguing enrichment of the methyltransferase in the Wnt7b upstream regions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: RNA-DNA-FISH results are shown in Figure 4D.

claim: ChIP assay showed enrichment of G9a in the Wnt7b upstream regions.
source: To test whether Lnc-Rewind and G9a binds the Wnt7b locus in vivo, we applied RNA-DNA-FISH (Figure 4D) and a chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), respectively. In agreement with our hypothesis, we found an overlap between Lnc-Rewind (RNA) and Wnt7b (DNA) localization (Figure 4D) and an intriguing enrichment of the methyltransferase in the Wnt7b upstream regions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: ChIP experiment results are shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: H3K9me2 deposition decreased upon Lnc-Rewind knockdown at the Wnt7b locus.
source: Consistent with a role of Lnc-Rewind in the G9a-mediated epigenetic repression of Wnt7b, quantification of the H3K9me2 mark on the G9a-occupied genomic regions (Figure 4E, upper panel) showed that H3K9me2 deposition decreased upon Lnc-Rewind knockdown, compared to the GAP-SCR control (Figure 4E, lower panel).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K9me2 is shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Combined Lnc-Rewind (RNA)/Wnt7b (DNA) FISH/G9a (PROTEIN) immunostaining showed the colocalization of both G9a and Lnc-Rewind on Wnt7b genomic locus.
source: Moreover, a combined Lnc-Rewind (RNA)/Wnt7b (DNA) FISH/G9a (PROTEIN) immunostaining approach showed the colocalization of both G9a and Lnc-Rewind on Wnt7b genomic locus (Figure 5A).
evidence: Combined FISH/immunostaining results are shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Lnc-Rewind represses Wnt7b gene transcription by mediating the specific G9a-dependent H3K9me2 deposition on its locus during the proliferation phase of satellite cells.
source: In sum, our results support a mechanism of action through which Lnc-Rewind mediates G9a recruitment on Wnt7b locus to silence it through the deposition of the repressive mark H3K9me2 during the proliferation phase of satellite cells (Figure 5B), thus providing unique insights on the contribution of nuclear-enriched lncRNAs in myogenesis.
evidence: This mechanism is supported by multiple experiments (RIP, CLIP, RNA pulldown, ChIP) and illustrated in the model in Figure 5B.

claim: The majority of the genomic content is pervasively transcribed into a diverse range of regulatory short and long non-protein coding RNAs (ncRNAs).
source: The transcriptional output of all organisms was recently found to be more complex than originally imagined, as the majority of the genomic content is pervasively transcribed into a diverse range of regulatory short and long non-protein coding RNAs (ncRNAs) (Abugessaisa et al., 2017; Carninci et al., 2005; Cipriano and Ballarino, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are operationally defined as transcripts longer than 200 nucleotides, which display little or no protein coding potential.
source: Among them, long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are operationally defined as transcripts longer than 200 nucleotides, which display little or no protein coding potential.
evidence: This is a standard definition in the field.

claim: Numerous studies have demonstrated lncRNAs' contribution to many biological processes, including pluripotency, cell differentiation, and organism development.
source: Since the initial discovery, numerous studies have demonstrated their contribution to many biological processes, including pluripotency, cell differentiation, and organism development (Ballarino et al., 2016; Fatica and Bozzoni, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: LncRNAs were demonstrated to regulate gene expression at transcriptional, post-transcriptional, or translational level.
source: LncRNAs were demonstrated to regulate gene expression at transcriptional, post-transcriptional, or translational level.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The function and the mechanisms of action of lncRNAs are different and primarily depend on their (nuclear or cytoplasmic) subcellular localization.
source: The function and the mechanisms of action are different and primarily depend on their (nuclear or cytoplasmic) subcellular localization (Carlevaro et al., 2019; Rinn and Chang, 2012; Ulitsky and Bartel, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A large number of lncRNAs localize inside the nucleus, either enriched on the chromatin or restricted to specific nucleoplasmic foci.
source: A large number of lncRNAs localize inside the nucleus, either enriched on the chromatin or restricted to specific nucleoplasmic foci (Engreitz et al., 2016; Sun et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Nuclear lncRNAs have the capacity to control the expression of neighbouring (in cis) or distant (in trans) genes by regulating their chromatin environment and also acting as structural scaffolds of nuclear domains.
source: In this location, they have the capacity to control the expression of neighbouring (in cis) or distant (in trans) genes by regulating their chromatin environment and also acting as structural scaffolds of nuclear domains (Kopp and Mendell, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Among the most important functions proposed for cis-acting lncRNAs, there is their ability to regulate transcription by recruiting repressing or activating epigenetic complexes to specific genomic loci.
source: Among the most important functions proposed for cis-acting lncRNAs, there is their ability to regulate transcription by recruiting repressing or activating epigenetic complexes to specific genomic loci (Huarte et al., 2010; Maamar et al., 2013; McHugh et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: High-throughput transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) and differential expression analyses have facilitated the discovery of several lncRNAs that are modulated during the different stages of skeletal myogenesis and dysregulated in muscle disorders.
source: In muscle, high-throughput transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) and differential expression analyses have facilitated the discovery of several lncRNAs that are modulated during the different stages of skeletal myogenesis and dysregulated in muscle disorders (Ballarino et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2013; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The lncRNA Lnc-mg has been shown to regulate MuSC differentiation by acting as a sponge for Mir125b in the cytoplasm.
source: In the cytoplasm, the lncRNA Lnc-mg has been shown to regulate MuSC differentiation by acting as a sponge for Mir125b (Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The lncRNA Dubr was found to promote satellite cell differentiation by recruiting Dnmts to the developmental pluripotency-associated 2 (Dppa2) promoter, leading to CpG hypermethylation and silencing in the nucleus.
source: In the nucleus, the lncRNA Dubr was found to promote satellite cell differentiation by recruiting Dnmts to the developmental pluripotency-associated 2 (Dppa2) promoter, leading to CpG hypermethylation and silencing (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The WNT transduction cascade has been demonstrated to act as a conserved regulator of stem cell function via canonical (β-CATENIN) and non-canonical (planar cell polarity and calcium) signalling.
source: The WNT transduction cascade has been demonstrated to act as a conserved regulator of stem cell function via canonical (β-CATENIN) and non-canonical (planar cell polarity and calcium) signalling, and dysregulation of its activity has been reported in various developmental disorders and diseases (Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Dysregulation of WNT signalling activity has been reported in various developmental disorders and diseases.
source: The WNT transduction cascade has been demonstrated to act as a conserved regulator of stem cell function via canonical (β-CATENIN) and non-canonical (planar cell polarity and calcium) signalling, and dysregulation of its activity has been reported in various developmental disorders and diseases (Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: In the muscle stem cell niche, WNT signalling is key in coordinating MuSC transitions from quiescence, proliferation, commitment, and differentiation.
source: In the muscle stem cell niche, WNT signalling is key in coordinating MuSC transitions from quiescence, proliferation, commitment, and differentiation (Brack et al., 2008; Eliazer et al., 2019; Lacour et al., 2017; Le Grand et al., 2009; Parisi et al., 2015; Rudolf et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: Different works have shown that lncRNAs can modulate the WNT pathway at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels.
source: Because of this central role, the WNT pathway is supervised by several mechanisms and different works have shown that lncRNAs can modulate it at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels (Zarkou et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Most of the cis-acting chromatin-associated lncRNA function occurs by recruiting and guiding chromatin modifiers to target genes.
source: Several works accumulated so far indicate that most of the cis-acting chromatin-associated lncRNA function occurs by recruiting and guiding chromatin modifiers to target genes (Batista and Chang, 2013; Guttman and Rinn, 2012; Khalil et al., 2009; Rinn and Chang, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple previous studies.

claim: EZH2 catalyses the deposition of H3K27me3 on target genes.
source: In light of our data showing a negative correlation of Wnt7b expression by Lnc-Rewind, we focused our attention on the two most known repressive lysine methyltransferases, EZH2 and G9a, which catalyse the deposition of H3K27me3 and H3K9me1/2 on target genes, respectively (Mozzetta et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: G9a catalyses the deposition of H3K9me1/2 on target genes.
source: In light of our data showing a negative correlation of Wnt7b expression by Lnc-Rewind, we focused our attention on the two most known repressive lysine methyltransferases, EZH2 and G9a, which catalyse the deposition of H3K27me3 and H3K9me1/2 on target genes, respectively (Mozzetta et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Wnt signalling represents one of the pathways that has a major role in myogenesis as it is essential for proper MuSC self-renewal and differentiation.
source: Wnt signalling represents one of the pathways that has a major role in myogenesis as it is essential for proper MuSC self-renewal and differentiation (von Maltzahn et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: A correct timing of Wnt signalling activation is crucial to obtain proper tissue repair.
source: A correct timing of Wnt signalling activation is crucial to obtain proper tissue repair, and its aberrant activity causes a wide range of pathologies (Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Aberrant Wnt signalling activity causes a wide range of pathologies.
source: A correct timing of Wnt signalling activation is crucial to obtain proper tissue repair, and its aberrant activity causes a wide range of pathologies (Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Recent studies show that lncRNAs can modulate Wnt pathway by affecting gene expression through different mechanisms, from transcriptional to post-transcriptional level.
source: Recent studies show that lncRNAs can modulate Wnt pathway by affecting gene expression through different mechanisms, from transcriptional to post-transcriptional level (Ong et al., 2017; Shen et al., 2017; Zarkou et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: LncRNAs were found interacting with transcription factors and chromatin modifiers altering Wnt signalling pathway in different tissues and in cancer.
source: For example, lncRNAs were found interacting with transcription factors (Desideri et al., 2020) and chromatin modifiers (Hu et al., 2015) altering Wnt signalling pathway in different tissues and in cancer.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The slowness in the splicing process could contribute to the maintenance of Lnc-Rewind at its own site of transcription improving its retention on the chromatin.
source: The slowness in the splicing process could contribute to the maintenance of Lnc-Rewind at its own site of transcription improving its retention on the chromatin.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation of unspliced isoforms.

claim: Recent evidence indicates that the presence of introns, and their distinct processing, may represent a way to regulate the nuclear localization and function of many lncRNAs.
source: In line with this, recent evidence indicates that the presence of introns, and their distinct processing, may represent a way to regulate the nuclear localization and function of many lncRNAs (Guo et al., 2020; Zuckerman and Ulitsky, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: The repressive action of Lnc-Rewind on Wnt7b locus could have a more general role, not only in satellite cells.
source: Moreover, we show that Lnc-Rewind and Wnt7b expressions are anti-correlated in different cell types (Figure 3B), suggesting that the repressive action of Lnc-Rewind on Wnt7b locus could have a more general role, not only in satellite cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the anti-correlation observed across multiple cell types in FANTOM5 data (Figure 3B).

claim: It is well-accepted that the majority of the cis-acting chromatin-associated lncRNAs function by recruiting and targeting chromatin modifiers to specific genes.
source: It is well-accepted that the majority of the cis-acting chromatin-associated lncRNAs function by recruiting and targeting chromatin modifiers to specific genes (Batista and Chang, 2013; Guttman and Rinn, 2012; Khalil et al., 2009; Rinn and Chang, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Low β-catenin activity is fundamental during early phases of muscle regeneration to allow MuSC activation and subsequent differentiation.
source: For instance, it has been shown that low β-catenin activity is fundamental during early phases of muscle regeneration to allow MuSC activation and subsequent differentiation (Figeac and Zammit, 2015; Parisi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Satellite cells isolated from mice with constitutive active Wnt/β-catenin signalling display an early growth arrest and premature differentiation.
source: Accordingly, satellite cells isolated from mice with constitutive active Wnt/β-catenin signalling display an early growth arrest and premature differentiation (Rudolf et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The cell environment, together with the timing and the proper activation of Wnt signalling pathway, is fundamental for muscle homeostasis.
source: All these data point out that the cell environment, together with the timing and the proper activation of Wnt signalling pathway, is fundamental for muscle homeostasis.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited studies and the authors' data.

claim: The fact that in MuSCs, Wnt7b gene is maintained at very low levels and that it is the latest Wnt ligand induced after muscle injury suggests the necessity to keep it repressed to allow MuSC expansion.
source: The fact that in MuSCs, Wnt7b gene is maintained at very low levels and that it is the latest Wnt ligand induced after muscle injury (Polesskaya et al., 2003) suggests the necessity to keep it repressed to allow MuSC expansion.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of low Wnt7b levels and its late induction, supported by citation.

claim: Aberrant, cell-autonomous activation of Wnt7b expression upon Lnc-Rewind depletion causes defects in MuSC expansion and activation.
source: In line with this, here we show that aberrant, cell-autonomous activation of Wnt7b expression upon Lnc-Rewind depletion causes defects in MuSC expansion and activation (Figure 2E–G) that are abolished if the expression of Wnt7b is rescued to physiological levels (Figure 3D,E), emphasizing that Lnc-Rewind-mediated repression of Wnt7b is key in ensuring MuSC activity.
evidence: This is demonstrated by depletion and rescue experiments shown in Figures 2E-G and 3D,E.

claim: Lnc-Rewind-mediated repression of Wnt7b is key in ensuring MuSC activity.
source: In line with this, here we show that aberrant, cell-autonomous activation of Wnt7b expression upon Lnc-Rewind depletion causes defects in MuSC expansion and activation (Figure 2E–G) that are abolished if the expression of Wnt7b is rescued to physiological levels (Figure 3D,E), emphasizing that Lnc-Rewind-mediated repression of Wnt7b is key in ensuring MuSC activity.
evidence: This is demonstrated by rescue experiments shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: Lu and colleagues demonstrated that the YY1-associated muscle lincRNA (Yam-1) inhibits skeletal myogenesis through modulation of Mir715 expression, which in turn targets Wnt7b mRNA.
source: This is nicely supported by a previous study demonstrating that, in the cytoplasm, a Wnt7b/lncRNA circuitry controls the proliferation of C2C12 myoblasts. Specifically, Lu and colleagues demonstrated that the YY1-associated muscle lincRNA (Yam-1) inhibits skeletal myogenesis through modulation of Mir715 expression, which in turn targets Wnt7b mRNA (Lu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Skeletal muscle possesses an outstanding capacity to regenerate upon injury due to the adult muscle stem cell (MuSC) activity.
source: Skeletal muscle possesses an outstanding capacity to regenerate upon injury due to the adult muscle stem cell (MuSC) activity.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The ability of skeletal muscle to regenerate requires the proper balance between MuSC expansion and differentiation.
source: This ability requires the proper balance between MuSC expansion and differentiation, which is critical for muscle homeostasis and contributes, if deregulated, to muscle diseases.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The proper balance between MuSC expansion and differentiation is critical for muscle homeostasis.
source: This ability requires the proper balance between MuSC expansion and differentiation, which is critical for muscle homeostasis and contributes, if deregulated, to muscle diseases.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Deregulation of the balance between MuSC expansion and differentiation contributes to muscle diseases.
source: This ability requires the proper balance between MuSC expansion and differentiation, which is critical for muscle homeostasis and contributes, if deregulated, to muscle diseases.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Lnc-Rewind is a chromatin-associated long noncoding RNA.
source: Here, we functionally characterize a novel chromatin-associated long noncoding RNA (lncRNA), Lnc-Rewind, which is expressed in murine MuSCs and conserved in human.
evidence: This is demonstrated by subcellular fractionation (Figure 1D) and RNA-FISH (Figure 1E,F) showing nuclear and chromatin enrichment.

claim: ~70% reduction of Lnc-Rewind expression was obtained by LNA GapmeR treatment.
source: Under these conditions, we obtained ~70% reduction of Lnc-Rewind expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, lower panel), which led to the identification of a set of 1088 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) (p<0.05, GAP-SCR vs GAP-REW).
evidence: qRT-PCR quantification is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The GAP-SCR and GAP-REW experimental groups displayed a clear different pattern of gene expression in PCA analysis.
source: A principal component analysis (PCA) performed on the DEG datasets revealed that the GAP-SCR and GAP-REW experimental groups displayed a clear different pattern of gene expression since they occupy different regions of the PCA plot (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: PCA plot is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 'Muscle system process' (p-value=3.45E-7) and 'striated muscle contraction' (p-value=4.63E-7) were the most significantly enriched GO terms.
source: Both 'muscle system process' (p-value=3.45E-7) and 'striated muscle contraction' (p-value=4.63E-7) were the most significantly enriched GO terms (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: GO enrichment analysis results are shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: None of the upregulated transcripts that are also putative Mirlet7b and Mirlet7c-2 targets belong to any of the GO enriched categories.
source: Of note, the analysis of Lnc-Rewind generated miRNAs (Mirlet7b and Mirlet7c-2) revealed that, although the lncRNA depletion results on their concomitant downregulation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), none of the upregulated transcripts that are also putative Mirlet7b and Mirlet7c-2 targets (~1% of the upregulated genes) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), belong to any of the GO enriched categories.
evidence: Target prediction analysis is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The defects in myogenic capacity might result from a decreased cell density that normally leads to a lower rate of myogenic differentiation.
source: This led us to hypothesize that the defects in myogenic capacity (Figure 2C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) might result by a decreased cell density that normally leads to a lower rate of myogenic differentiation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation of decreased cell numbers (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).

claim: Cyclin D3 is a cyclin specifically involved in promoting transition from G1 to S phase.
source: Accordingly, the Ccnd3 gene encoding for Cyclin D3, a cyclin specifically involved in promoting transition from G1 to S phase, was significantly downregulated in Lnc-Rewind-depleted cells at both transcript (Figure 2—source data 1) and protein levels (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Cyclin D3 function.

claim: Lnc-Rewind has a role in sustaining MuSC activation and expansion.
source: Moreover, quantification of the number of Pax7+-derived clusters (composed of more than two nuclei), pairs (composed of two nuclei), or single MuSCs within each myofibre revealed a reduction of activated pairs and clusters upon Lnc-Rewind depletion (Figure 2G), suggesting a role for the lncRNA in sustaining MuSC activation and expansion.
evidence: This is inferred from the quantification data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The genomic proximity between Lnc-Rewind/Wnt7b loci, together with their anti-correlated expression in muscle cells and the lncRNA chromatin enrichment, suggests that Lnc-Rewind might have a direct, in cis-regulatory role on Wnt7b transcription.
source: The genomic proximity between Lnc-Rewind/Wnt7b loci, together with their anti-correlated expression in muscle cells and the lncRNA chromatin enrichment (Figure 1D,E), led us to hypothesize that Lnc-Rewind might have a direct, in cis-regulatory role on Wnt7b transcription.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on genomic proximity, expression correlation, and chromatin localization data.

claim: Lnc-Rewind acts as a repressor of Wnt7b expression.
source: Among them, we found Wnt7b, which expression was found upregulated at both transcript and protein levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and Figure 2—source data 1), suggesting a role for Lnc-Rewind as a repressor of Wnt7b expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the upregulation of Wnt7b upon Lnc-Rewind depletion.

claim: The Kcnq1ot1 lncRNA was previously demonstrated to be physically associated with both G9a and Ezh2 proteins.
source: To note, the levels of RNA obtained in the specific IP fraction were similar to the ones of the Kcnq1ot1 lncRNA, which was previously demonstrated to be physically associated with both G9a and Ezh2 proteins (Pandey et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In Lnc-Rewind CLIP, Lnc-Rewind RNA-specific enrichment was comparable to the Kcnq1ot1-positive control.
source: As for RIP, also in this case, Lnc-Rewind RNA-specific enrichment was comparable to the Kcnq1ot1-positive control.
evidence: This is shown in the CLIP experiment in Figure 4A.

claim: The histone H3K9 lysine methyltransferase (KMT) might be specifically tethered on Wnt7b genomic locus by Lnc-Rewind to mediate its transcriptional repression.
source: This strongly suggests that the histone H3K9 lysine methyltransferase (KMT) might be specifically tethered on Wnt7b genomic locus by Lnc-Rewind to mediate its transcriptional repression.
evidence: This is inferred from the interaction data (RIP, CLIP, RNA pulldown) and the functional data (G9a knockdown, ChIP).

claim: Different regions upstream Wnt7b locus are enriched in the G9a-deposited histone mark H3K9me2 in MuSC-derived myoblasts.
source: In support of this idea, through H3K9me2 ChIP experiments here we provide evidence that different regions upstream Wnt7b locus are enriched in the G9a-deposited histone mark in MuSC-derived myoblasts and that H3K9me2 levels on these regions significantly decrease upon Lnc-Rewind knockdown (Figure 4E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data is shown in Figure 4E.

claim: H3K9me2 levels on regions upstream Wnt7b locus significantly decrease upon Lnc-Rewind knockdown.
source: In support of this idea, through H3K9me2 ChIP experiments here we provide evidence that different regions upstream Wnt7b locus are enriched in the G9a-deposited histone mark in MuSC-derived myoblasts and that H3K9me2 levels on these regions significantly decrease upon Lnc-Rewind knockdown (Figure 4E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data is shown in Figure 4E.

claim: G9a downregulation is sufficient to induce Wnt7b de-repression.
source: These data, together with the evidence that G9a downregulation is sufficient to induce Wnt7b de-repression (Figure 4C), confirm a direct role for G9a-mediated H3K9 methylation in maintaining the repression of Wnt7b in MuSCs.
evidence: qRT-PCR data showing Wnt7b upregulation upon G9a knockdown is shown in Figure 4C.

claim: G9a-mediated H3K9 methylation has a direct role in maintaining the repression of Wnt7b in MuSCs.
source: These data, together with the evidence that G9a downregulation is sufficient to induce Wnt7b de-repression (Figure 4C), confirm a direct role for G9a-mediated H3K9 methylation in maintaining the repression of Wnt7b in MuSCs.
evidence: This is inferred from multiple lines of evidence including G9a knockdown (Figure 4C), ChIP (Figure 4E), and interaction studies.
